title: biscuit
summary: A crunchy treat with an old baking instruction hidden inside.
question: What cooking instruction is hidden in biscuit?
completion: You followed biscuit through French bescuit to medieval Latin biscoctum, then found bis (twice) and coctus (cooked/baked). Italian biscotto is a relative. The old name describes twice-baked bread; today’s biscuits need not all be baked twice.
partner: Follow the sounds, places and meanings. What surprising connection will you discover?
